name: Page your on-call team on WhatsApp until someone answers with Turbo Notify

nodes.name: Receive an alert
nodes.notes: Needs Header Auth: a request without the right header is refused and never reaches the workflow. n8n normally assigns a new address to an imported copy: use the Production URL shown in this node. Share it and the header value only with your monitoring tool, over HTTPS.

nodes.name: Poll WhatsApp replies
nodes.notes: Reads the replies of your on-call people once a minute. Works on every plan. A reply written while n8n was off is read at the next poll.

nodes.name: Every minute: look for unanswered alerts
nodes.notes: Every minute it pages the next level of any alert that was not taken in time. It does nothing when no alert is open. It counts as one n8n execution a minute: see the README before you keep it on n8n Cloud, and set 2 or 5 minutes if you prefer.

assignments.name: ack_words
assignments.value: ok, ack, got it, visto, ciente

assignments.name: msg_escalated
assignments.value: ESCALATED, nobody answered level {previous_level}. [{severity}] {service}: {message}\nReply OK {code} to take it.

assignments.name: msg_ack_note
assignments.value: {name} took {service} ({code}). You do not need to act.

assignments.name: msg_final
assignments.value: Nobody acknowledged {service} ({code}): {message}\nNo more messages will follow for this alert. Check it now.

nodes.name: Your settings
nodes.notes:
oncall_phone_1: level 1, paged first. With + and country code. NEVER the phone linked to Turbo Notify: it cannot page itself. Replace it: the workflow stops while it is a placeholder
oncall_phone_2: level 2, paged when level 1 does not answer. Another person's real number, never the linked phone. Empty it to use fewer levels. On Free, at most two different phones in all: set owner_phone equal to this one, or empty this
oncall_phone_3: level 3, optional. Leave empty for two levels. Not the linked phone
owner_phone: gets the final message when nobody answers. Not the linked phone either. May be the same number as a level, which on Free keeps you at two phones
ack_minutes: minutes a level has to answer. The timer adds one minute of grace and runs every minute, so the next level is paged ack_minutes + 1 to + 2 minutes after the page. With a slower Schedule Trigger use a multiple of its interval
ack_words: a reply that starts with one of these takes the alert, optionally followed by its code (OK 7K2F). Comma separated, capitals and accents do not matter
min_severity: alerts below this severity are ignored. An unknown or missing severity is never ignored
severity_order: your severities from the lowest to the highest, comma separated. The highest one is never held back by max_new_alerts_per_hour
max_new_alerts_per_hour: more new alerts than this in the last 60 minutes are not paged and the run fails, so a flood is seen. The block is rolling: it lifts as alerts age past the hour
reopen_minutes: an alert that fires again less than this long after it was resolved is ignored (a monitor that flaps). At least 1 minute. If your tool only reports changes, a second outage inside this time is not paged: set 0 or 1
rearm_hours: an alert that was taken or that nobody took pages again if it fires again after this many hours
max_text_length: longest alert message accepted. Longer text is cut. Service names are cut at 80
field_alert_id: name of the field in your alert that holds a unique id or fingerprint. Without one the same service and text count as the same alert
field_service: name of the field with the service or host
field_severity: name of the field with the severity
field_status: name of the field with firing or resolved (empty or any other word means firing)
field_message: name of the field with the text of the alert. Do not put secrets or customer data in it
field_runbook_url: name of the field with a link to the runbook, optional. It is added to the page text and gives the page a button
runbook_button_text: text on the runbook button, at most 20 characters
msg_page: the first page. {service} {severity} {message} {code} {alert_id} {minutes}. \n is a line break. The runbook link is added at the end
msg_escalated: the page of the next level. Same placeholders, plus {previous_level} and {level}
msg_ack_confirm: sent to the person who took the alert. Same placeholders as msg_page
msg_ack_note: sent to the other levels already paged. Same placeholders, plus {name}: the name WhatsApp shows, or the number
msg_final: sent once to every level and to the owner after the last level did not answer. Same placeholders as msg_page
msg_resolved: sent to the people who were paged when the monitoring tool reports the alert resolved. Same placeholders as msg_page

nodes.name: Check the settings
nodes.notes: Stops the run while a phone is a placeholder or a setting makes no sense. Then it hands on what the trigger delivered.

nodes.name: Webhook alert, or replies and timer?
nodes.notes: True: an alert from your monitoring tool. False: replies from the poll, or the minute timer.

nodes.name: Find the alert in the table
nodes.notes: Reads the row of this alert and the alerts opened in the last hour (to count a flood).

nodes.name: Decide what to do with the alert
nodes.notes: Checks and caps the fields, ignores low severities and repeated firing, closes on resolved, opens a new incident otherwise. An alert with an odd id or no id is still paged.

nodes.name: Save the alert
nodes.notes: The alert is stored BEFORE anybody is paged, so a restart cannot lose it.

nodes.name: Read the open alerts
nodes.notes: Reads the alerts that are still open, once per run.

nodes.name: Decide what each open alert needs
nodes.notes: After a poll: matches each reply to the alert it takes. On the timer: finds the alerts that need the next level, one minute after ack_minutes.

nodes.name: Write the messages
nodes.notes: The one place that decides who gets which message, from the wording in Your settings.

nodes.name: Does the page carry a runbook button?
nodes.notes: True: a page for an alert that has a runbook link.

nodes.name: Send the page with the runbook button
nodes.notes: One message with a button that opens the runbook. Tried up to 3 times when the first message of a batch is refused (the idempotency key makes a repeat safe). If it is still refused the run goes on and the row records why.

nodes.name: Send the text message
nodes.notes: Every other message. Tried up to 3 times when the first message of a batch is refused (the idempotency key makes a repeat safe). If it is still refused the run goes on and the row records why.

nodes.name: Gather the answers of Turbo Notify
nodes.notes: Puts the answers of both send nodes back together.

nodes.name: Update the alert rows
nodes.notes: Matches each answer with its message and keeps only the columns this run owns (a page writes the level, an acknowledgement writes who took it), so a slow run cannot undo another.

nodes.name: Save the alert after sending
nodes.notes: Writes the new level, the message id, the status where this run owns it, and any failure. Columns the run does not own are left as they are.

nodes.name: Report what failed
nodes.notes: Fails the run when any message was refused, naming the alert, the phone and the reason. This is what your Error workflow reacts to.

parameters.content:
### How it works
A WhatsApp page next to your paging tool. Your monitoring tool posts a JSON alert to a protected webhook.

The workflow pages on-call level 1 with the service, the severity, a 4 character code and, when the alert has a link, a runbook button. A reply such as "OK 7K2F" takes the alert and tells the other levels.

If nobody answers within ack_minutes the next level is paged, then one final message goes to everybody. A resolved alert closes it. WhatsApp is an extra channel, not a paging service.

### Setup
1. Install [@turbo-notify/n8n-nodes-turbo-notify](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@turbo-notify/n8n-nodes-turbo-notify) (tested 1.5.15). Verified community node: installs from the nodes panel on n8n Cloud and from Settings > Community Nodes on self-hosted n8n.
2. Create a Turbo Notify API credential (scopes messages:send and events:read) and a Header Auth credential "Alert access (Header Auth)".
3. Select the credentials on the Webhook, the Polling Trigger and both send nodes.
4. Run the manual branch once.
5. In Your settings type the on-call and owner numbers (none may be the phone linked to Turbo Notify).
6. POST a JSON alert with a required alert_id to the Production URL over HTTPS, then activate.

### Customization
Texts, severities and times are in Your settings. On a small plan, slow the one-minute timer down.

## Three ways in

An alert from your monitoring tool, a reply from your on-call people, and a timer every minute.

## Your settings

Every value you change lives in this node.

## Check, then route

Stops on a placeholder, then sends an alert one way and replies or the timer the other.

## Decide what is needed

A new alert opens or closes an incident, a reply takes one, and the timer finds the alert nobody took.

## Write and send

One place writes every message. A refused send never stops the others.

## Record and report

Each alert row keeps the message id or the failure. The run fails if nobody could be paged.

## Run once: create the table

Creates oncall_alerts when it is missing. Safe to run again.
**Replace the phone numbers before you activate.** While one is a placeholder the workflow stops and pages nobody.
